description_en: This temple is situated within the Gorakhanātha complex on the eastern bank of the Bagmati river. Rising on three plinth levels, the stone temple is surmounted by a bell-shaped roof adorned with a metallic finial. It boasts entrances on all four sides, each embellished with a stone archway (toraṇa) featuring a central carving of Chepu, a mythical water creature.Inside the sanctum, a central stoneśivaliṅgarepresenting Narendreśvara Mahādeva serves as the main deity, accompanied by four other deities aligned with the Śiva Pāñcāyana concept. Notably, the arrangement of these deities does not adhere to the conventional concept. Sūrya and Viṣṇu, typically placed in their respective corners, have been interchanged to inhabit the northeastern and southeastern niches. Gaṇeśa and Durgā, on the other hand, retain their customary positions in the southwest and northwest corners. A Bhairava mask is  embedded in the southern exterior wall—a characteristic feature of Śiva temples of this nature. Adjacent to the temple's southern side, a bell, installed in the year 1886 CE (VS 1943), hangs on a bell-stand. Anotherśivaliṅga(PPK1953-006) is positioned to the southwest, marking the site where the ascetic Viṣṇunātha Yogī was entombed. Additionally, a faded inscription west of the temple suggests an antiquity predating the temple's construction.Known colloquially as Salyānī Mahārānī (translated as the queen of Salyāna, a district in West Nepal), Toraṇadivyeśvarīdevī commissioned the construction of Narendreśvara Mandira in memory of her late husband, Narendra Bahādura Śāha, in the year 1881 CE (VS 1938) (G. Ṭaṇḍana VS 2053, p.351; Michaels and Tandon 2017, p.106). King of Salyāna, he ascended the throne in 1848 CE (VS 1905) following the demise of his father, Teja Bahādura Śāha (R. Gautama VS 2042, p.59). Post the temple's completion, Toraṇadivyeśvarīdevī, in the same year, donated land for the perpetual observance of rituals at this temple, as well as at the Gorakhanātha and Dhīramukteśvara temples (cf.K_0040_0020). Furthermore, in 1886 CE (VS 1943), she facilitated the installation of a bell at the temple. Later, the earthquakes of 2015 inflicted damage upon the temple, necessitating restoration efforts by the Pashupati Area Development Trust in 2021 CE (VS 2078).Daily rituals at the temple are conducted by a Brahmin from the Ghimire caste. However, as of November 2023, these rituals are irregularly observed due to the priest's inadequate compensation for his services.
description_ne: सल्यानी महारानी तोरणदिव्येश्वरीदेवीले आफ्ना श्रीमान् नरेन्द्रबहादुर शाहको नाममा  विसं १९३८ (सन् १८८१) मा यो शिवालय स्थापना गरी पूजाआजाको लागि जग्गा राखिदिएकी थिइन् ।पशुपति क्षेत्रमा रहेको गोरखनाथ परिसरमा यो शिवालय अवस्थित रहेको छ । तीन तहको ढुङ्गाको पेटीमाथि बनाइएको घण्टाकारको यस शिवालयमा धातुको गजूर राखिएको छ । शिवालयका चारै दिशामा ढोका बनाइएका छन् । ती ढोकामाथि छेपु अङ्कित ढुङ्गाका तोरण राखिएका छन् । यस शिवालयको गर्भगृहभित्र नरेन्द्रेश्वर शिवलिङ्ग स्थापना गरिएको छ । पद्धतिमा बनाइएको यस शिवालयको गर्भगृहभित्र पाञ्चायन देवीदेवताहरू स्थापना गरिएका छन्, तर पाञ्चायन पद्धतिअनुसार दिशा मिलेको देखिँदैन । उत्तर-पश्चिममा दुर्गा, उत्तर-पूर्वमा सूर्य, दक्षिण-पूर्वमा विष्णु र दक्षिण-पश्चिममा गणेशका मूर्ति स्थापना गरिएका छन् । मन्दिरको दक्षिणपट्टि भित्तामा भैरवको मुखाकृति राखिएको छ । शिवालयको दक्षिणमा विसं १९४३ (सन् १८८६) मा चढाइएको घण्टा रहेको छ । शिवालयको दक्षिण-पश्चिमपट्टि विष्णुनाथ योगीको समाधिमाथि बनाइएको शिवलिङ्ग (PPK1953-006) स्थापना गरिएको छ । त्यस्तै शिवालयको पश्चिममा खम्बा, गजूर र नन्दीका अवशेष पनि स्थापना गरिएका छन् । ती अवशेषसँगै एउटा शिलापत्र पनि ठड्याएको छ । अक्षर खिइएर बुझ्न नसकिने अवस्थाको भएपनि त्यसमा बाँकी रहेका केही अक्षरहरू हेर्दा उक्त शिलालेख शिवालय स्थापना हुनुभन्दा अगाडिको देखिन्छ ।यो शिवालय विसं १९३८ पौष कृष्ण ५ (सन् १८८१) मा तोरणदिव्येश्वरीदेवीले स्थापना गरेकी थिइन् (G. Ṭaṇḍana VS 2053, p.351; Michaels and Tandon 2017, p.106) । उनी सल्यानी महारानी थिइन् । सल्यानका राजा नरेन्द्रबहादुर शाहसँग उनको विवाह भएको थियो । सल्यानका राजा तेजबहादुर शाहको विसं १९०५ (सन् १८४८) मा देहावसान भएपछि उनका छोरा नरेन्द्रबहादुर शाह सल्यानका राजा भएका थिए (R. Gautama VS 2042, p.59) । महारानी तोरणदिव्येश्वरीदेवीले आफ्ना श्रीमान् नरेन्द्रबहादुर शाहको नाममा यो शिवालय स्थापना गरिसकेपछि यो शिवालय लगायत गोरखनाथ मन्दिर र धीरमुक्तेश्वर मन्दिरमा पनि धार्मिक पूजाविधि चलिरहोस् भन्ने अभिप्रायले विसं १९३८ (सन् १८८१) मा नै जग्गा दान दिएकी थिइन् (cf.K_0040_0020) । त्यसको केही वर्षपछि विसं १९४३ (१८८६) मा उनै महारानीले शिवालयको दक्षिणमा घण्टा चढाएकी थिइन् । विसं २०७२ (सन् २०१५) को भूकम्पले शिवालयमा क्षति पुगेपछि विसं २०७८ (सन् २०२१) मा पशुपति क्षेत्र विकास कोषले जीर्णोद्धार गरेको थियो ।यो शिवालयमा घिमिरे थरका ब्राह्मणले नित्यपूजा गरिरहेका छन् । उनलाई न्यून पारिश्रमिक दिइने गरिएकोले नियमित पूजा भइरहेको छैन ।

historical_events.event_description: Toraṇadivyeśvarīdevī consecrated the mainśivaliṅgain honor of her husband Narendra Bahādura Śāha.

Post the temple's completion, Toraṇadivyeśvarīdevī, in the same year, generously donated land for the perpetual observance of rituals at this temple, as well as at the Gorakhanātha and Dhīramukteśvara temples.
Salyānī Mahārānī Toraṇadivyeśvarīdevī installed a bell at the temple.
Anotherśivaliṅga(PPK1953-006) is established to the southwest of the temple, marking the site where the ascetic Viṣṇunātha Yogī was entombed.
The Pashupati Area Development Trust restored the temple following the damage inflicted upon it by the earthquakes of 2015.

Taking into account the discernible letters, the faded inscription located west of the temple implies an age predating the temple's construction. Despite the unclear content of the inscription, it appears that its installation may not be directly associated with the temple.
